senses.gloss: ris, a measure of length, 2/15 of a mile (stadium).
units: <cite ref="Bava Metzia 33a:5">B. Mets. 33ᵃ</cite> (Ar. <cite ref="T00411"><he>רוס</he></cite>, expl. as numerical value <he>רו״ס</he> = 266 cubits).
B. Kam. VII, 7 (79ᵇ) שלשים ר׳ thirty ris (four miles). Ib. 83ᵃ; a. fr.

<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:3:1">Cant. R. to I, 3</cite> <he>בית מדרשו … כמין ר׳</he> the college hall of R. El. was shaped like an arena (an oblong with seats on both sides).—Pl. <he>רִיסִים</he>. Y. B. Mets. V, 10ᶜ bot. (in Chald. dict.) <he>אילין דמפרשין לר׳</he>, v. <cite ref="S01643"><he>קסוסטבן</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Bekhorot 6:2">Bekh. VI, 2</cite> (<cite ref="Bekhorot 38a">38ᵃ</cite>), v. <cite ref="H01690"><he>חָרִיץ</he></cite>.

Bekh. 38ᵇ top מאי הר׳ … תורא וכ׳ what is haris?… The outer row of the eye. Sifra Emor, ch. VI, Par. 7 (expl. חרוץ, Lev. XXII, 22) ר׳ של עיניו וכ׳ one whose eye-lid is perforated, nipped, or split.—Pl. as ab., constr. רִיסֵי.
<cite ref="Bekhorot 43b:10">Bekh. 43ᵇ</cite> <he>שנשרו ר׳ עיניו</he> whose eye-lids are hairless.
<cite ref="Kiddushin 31a:2">Kidd. 31ᵃ</cite> <he>מבין ר׳ עיניך וכ׳</he> from thy eye-lids can be seen that thou art a widow’s son.
<cite ref="Horayot 12a:13">Hor. 12ᵃ</cite> <he>נותנין … ר׳ עיניו</he> they put the oil of anointment between his eye-lids; a. fr.
